messages:
eva: heads up — seeing a spike in fncall schema rejects for tool `search` in prod. console shows them all as "reject" which increments quota and triggers fallback to the degen model. is that expected? example payload that failed validation:
```json
{
  "fn_name": "search",
  "args": ["how to tune batching", "lang:en"]  // validator expects an OBJECT for args, got ARRAY
}
```

mike: how widespread is the spike? link to the dashboard? :eyes:

eva: ~1.2k rejects in the last 10m, ~60% from high-tier orgs. dashboard: /app/dashboards/fncall-rejects (will paste screenshot in thread).

prashant: are these strict schema rejects (enum/required) or parse errors?

eva: validator type = InvalidShape (array vs object). it's currently treated as a hard reject. that increments rejection_count and triggers fallback routing + billing increment.

sophia: we flipped the strict gate on fncall validation during the last rollout (flag fncall.strict.canary). could be the canary ramp.

prashant: suggestion: introduce a new outcome `soft_reject` for non-actionable shape mismatches. semantics: return original model output to caller (no automatic retry/fallback), mark telemetry with error tag, DO NOT increment quota/reject_count used for billing. add sampling + audit logs.

mike: billing team will push back if we stop counting rejects. also potential for customers to game it to avoid enforcement.

prashant: mitigations: only apply soft_reject when validator confidence < 0.7 AND the mismatch is structural (eg array vs object) not a malicious payload. require org-level opt-in/opt-out toggle for strict enforcement. add sampling (1% full payloads) for manual audits.

sophia: console UX requests: show a separate panel for `soft_rejects` with example payloads, allow one-click "replay with strict enforcement" to reproduce, and expose rate by org + route id.

deploy-bot: toggle fncall.strict.canary set to 10% by sophia at 5172468900.

mike: :thumbsup: can we also emit a lightweight metric `fncall_soft_reject_rate` and a delta to token billing in the telemetry pipeline? ops needs to monitor cost drift.

eva: yes please. we need alerts if soft_reject_rate > 5% for top 50 orgs.

prashant: i'll open a design doc + PR. proposed plan:
1) validator: add outcome enum {accept, soft_reject, hard_reject}
2) routing: soft_reject -> do not route to fallback layer, preserve response to caller
3) telemetry: emit soft_reject_rate, sample payloads for audit, include validator confidence and rule id
4) console: add panel and replay tool
5) billing: add contract to keep soft_reject non-billable unless org opts in

sophia: rollout plan — canary 10% for 24h, monitor soft_reject_rate, downstream error delta, and customer feedback. promote to 100% after signoff from billing and SRE.

mike: tagging finance for awareness @finance (will loop them in).

eva: thanks all. sample id for triage: sample-9843 (ingest id). i'll attach logs and a raw req/resp.

infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-1242 to track validator change and telemetry plumbing. assigned to prashant.

prashant: i'll iterate on the doc and aim for a PR today. if anyone has concerns about gaming, drop examples here and we'll add heuristics.

sophia: agreed. let's keep the console visibility tight during canary.

eva: sounds good. will post follow-ups and screenshots. :thumbsup:
